correctness.rationale: Prime cyclotomic irreducibility makes a rational polynomial Σ_j d_j ζ^j vanish exactly when all p coefficients d_j coincide. At a=0,b≠0 the exponent permutes the field, hence vanishing is equivalent to f being constant; at (0,0) the sum must vanish. At a≠0 the quadratic exponent has only (p+1)/2 distinct outputs; at least one aggregate d_j=0, forcing all to zero and hence cancellation on every pair {t,s−t}, s=−b/a, plus zero at fixed point s/2. Two reflection-odd centers give invariance under a nonzero translation, forcing a nonzero f to be constant and simultaneously odd, impossible. Reflection uniqueness yields all four shapes. Sign support 2r can be balanced but nonreflection-odd (one origin zero), balanced reflection-odd (a unique p-point line), or unbalanced (zero zeros); counting support and reflection orbits yields the displayed binomial formulas. Independently enumerated all 3^5−1=242 and 3^7−1=2186 nonzero {-1,0,1} arrays, applying exact integer exponent bucket sums at every Fourier frequency: for p=5 classes 0:190,1:10,4:2,5:40, and p=7 classes 0:1792,1:210,6:2,7:182. The complete all-prime proof uses irreducibility and orbit counting, not the finite enumerations.
